mainTopic: נדר שהותר מקצתו according to רבה and רבא, and נדרי אונסין: whether a condition missed because of אונס still takes effect
overview: Before this amud, רבה and רבא argued about exactly where רבי עקיבא and רבנן disagree on a vow that was partly undone. The גמרא first finishes a ברייתא about a basket of figs that turned out to hold בנות שוח. It tries to use that ברייתא against רבא, and then defends רבא by reading the man's words as 'the whole basket is forbidden.' Next it asks who taught a ברייתא about a vow against five people, and shows how each part fits according to רבה and according to רבא. A new משנה then defines נדרי אונסין, meaning vows that could not be kept because of sickness or a river. In the גמרא, a man said his court documents would become void if he did not return in thirty days. He was held back by אונס, and רב הונא rules the documents are void. רבא disagrees, because the תורה exempts an אנוס, and he proves this applies even outside capital cases from our משנה. The גמרא then challenges רבא from a conditional גט where the husband died, and begins an answer that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The basket of figs ברייתא and רבי עקיבא's rule
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא ends: a person vowed off a basket that turned out to hold בנות שוח and said he would not have vowed had he known. At first the ruling was that the basket stays forbidden and only the בנות שוח are permitted. Then רבי עקיבא taught that a vow partly undone is fully undone.
steps.simpleTranslation: There were בנות שוח in the basket, and he said: 'Had I known there were בנות שוח inside, I would not have vowed.' The basket is forbidden and the בנות שוח are permitted. This held until רבי עקיבא came and taught: a vow that is partly undone is completely undone.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a ברייתא it began quoting earlier. It is setting up an attempt to prove something about רבא's view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier opinion (רבנן) says only the part he regrets becomes permitted. רבי עקיבא says that once any part of the vow is undone, the whole vow falls away. The next step asks exactly what the man said, to see whose view fits.

keyTerms.meaning: A vow that is partly undone is completely undone

phrases.english: and there were בנות שוח in it,
phrases.notes: "It" is the basket of figs he vowed not to eat from.

phrases.english: and he said: 'Had I known
that there were בנות שוח inside it,
I would not have vowed'
the basket is forbidden,
the בנות שוח are permitted.
Until רבי עקיבא came and taught:
a vow that was partly undone
is completely undone.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא quoted just before this section as a test of רבה and רבא.
steps.raayaObject: Where רבי עקיבא and רבנן disagree

steps.title: The ברייתא seems to go against רבא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests the man meant 'black and white figs forbidden, בנות שוח permitted,' which is the 'this one and that one' wording. Yet the ברייתא shows a מחלוקת there, while רבא said everyone agrees in that case.
steps.simpleTranslation: Isn't it that he said: 'Had I known there were בנות שוח inside, I would have said: black and white figs are forbidden, בנות שוח are permitted'? And this is רבי עקיבא, and רבנן disagree?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reads the ברייתא as using the 'list each kind' wording. That would challenge רבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Naming the black and white figs one by one is like saying 'this one and that one are forbidden.' רבא said everyone agrees all become permitted in that case. But here רבנן disagree with רבי עקיבא, so the ברייתא would contradict רבא.

keyTerms.meaning: Is it not that…? (a proposed reading used to push a point)

steps.confusionAlert: The challenge depends on the exact wording the man would have used. Listing items one by one and saying 'all except' are treated as two different cases.

phrases.english: What, is it not that he said:

phrases.aramaic: אִילּוּ הָיִיתִי יוֹדֵעַ שֶׁבְּנוֹת שׁוּחַ בְּתוֹכָהּ,
phrases.english: 'Had I known that there were בנות שוח inside it,
I would have said:
black and white figs are forbidden,
בנות שוח are permitted',
and this is רבי עקיבא,
and the Rabbis disagree?
phrases.notes: Left unsaid: רבא said everyone agrees in this kind of case, so this goes against him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws an inference from the ברייתא in step 1 against רבא.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's claim that with the 'this one and that one' wording, everyone agrees all become permitted
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the ברייתא is the 'list each kind' wording and still shows רבי עקיבא and רבנן disagreeing, then רבא's 'everyone agrees' is wrong.

steps.title: The man said 'the whole basket is forbidden'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the man meant 'the whole basket is forbidden and the בנות שוח are permitted.' That is the 'all except' wording, where רבא agrees there is a מחלוקת.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. The case is where he says: 'Had I known there were בנות שוח inside, I would have said: the whole basket is forbidden, and the בנות שוח are permitted.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבא by reading the man's words differently.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'The whole basket is forbidden, but the בנות שוח are permitted' is the 'all forbidden except this' wording. According to רבא, that is exactly where רבי עקיבא and רבנן disagree. So the ברייתא fits רבא after all.

keyTerms.meaning: In a case where he says

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבא, the basket ברייתא is the 'all forbidden except one' wording, and that is the case where רבי עקיבא and רבנן disagree.

phrases.english: No, it is where he says:

phrases.aramaic: אִילּוּ הָיִיתִי יוֹדֵעַ שֶׁבְּנוֹת שׁוּחַ בְּתוֹכָהּ,
phrases.english: 'Had I known that there were בנות שוח inside it,
I would have said:
the whole basket is forbidden,
and the בנות שוח are permitted'.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Re-defining the case (the exact wording the vower meant)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The man meant he would have listed black and white figs as forbidden.
steps.terutzMaskana: The man meant 'the whole basket forbidden except the בנות שוח,' which is רבא's case of מחלוקת.

steps.title: Who is the תנא of the five-people ברייתא?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא: someone vowed off five people in one statement. If the vow is undone for one, it is undone for all. If he said 'except for one of them,' only that one is permitted. Who taught this?
steps.simpleTranslation: Who is the תנא of what רבנן taught: If someone vowed in one statement not to benefit from five people, and the vow was undone for one of them, it is undone for all of them. If he said 'except for one of them,' that one is permitted and the others are forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new question. It asks whose opinion lies behind a ברייתא about a vow against five people, and sets up two answers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא has two parts that seem to follow opposite rules. In the first part, undoing one undoes all, like רבי עקיבא. In the second part, 'except for one' leaves the rest forbidden, like רבנן. The גמרא wants to know how each part fits.

keyTerms.meaning: Who is the תנא (who taught this)?

phrases.english: Who taught this
which the Rabbis taught:
if someone vowed against five people as one,
phrases.notes: He vowed not to benefit from any of them, all in one statement.

phrases.english: and it was undone for one of them,
they are all permitted.
'Except for one of them':
he is permitted, and they are forbidden.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to a new ברייתא to see how it fits רבה and רבא.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא, רבי עקיבא or רבנן, stands behind each part of the five-people ברייתא

steps.title: According to רבה: first part is רבי עקיבא, second part is everyone
steps.stepSummary: According to רבה, the first part (undone for one, undone for all) is רבי עקיבא. The second part ('except for one') is everyone's view.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you follow רבה: the first part is רבי עקיבא, and the second part is everyone's opinion.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the first answer, based on how רבה understands the מחלוקת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבה, 'this one and that one forbidden, this one permitted' is the case of מחלוקת. So the first part, where all become permitted, must be רבי עקיבא alone. 'All except one' is a case where everyone agrees the rest stay forbidden, so the second part is דברי הכל.

keyTerms.meaning: The first part of a teaching
The last part of a teaching

phrases.english: If according to רבה,
the first part is רבי עקיבא
and the last part is everyone's opinion.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 4 according to רבה.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: First part follows רבי עקיבא; second part is דברי הכל.

steps.title: According to רבא: second part is רבנן, first part is everyone
steps.stepSummary: According to רבא, the second part ('except for one') is רבנן. The first part (undone for one, undone for all) is everyone's view.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you follow רבא: the second part is רבנן, and the first part is everyone's opinion.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the second answer, based on how רבא understands the מחלוקת. It is the mirror image of רבה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבא, 'all except one' is the case of מחלוקת. So the second part, where the rest stay forbidden, is רבנן alone. With the 'this one and that one' wording, everyone agrees all become permitted, so the first part is דברי הכל.
steps.whatToRemember: The five-people ברייתא fits both views, just divided differently. For רבה, the first part is רבי עקיבא and the second part is everyone. For רבא, the second part is רבנן and the first part is everyone.

phrases.english: If according to רבא,
the last part is the Rabbis
and the first part is everyone's opinion.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the parallel answer according to רבא, the mirror image of step 5.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Second part follows רבנן; first part is דברי הכל.

steps.title: The משנה defines vows blocked by circumstances
steps.stepSummary: The משנה gives an example of נדרי אונסין: a friend made someone vow to eat at his house, and then sickness or a river stopped him from going.
steps.simpleTranslation: What are vows blocked by circumstances? If a person's friend bound him with a vow to eat at his house, and then he got sick, or his son got sick, or a river held him back, these are vows blocked by circumstances.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה opens. It gives a clear example of a vow that could not be kept because something outside the person's control got in the way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The person meant to keep the vow, but sickness or a flooded river stopped him. The משנה labels these נדרי אונסין, meaning such vows are not counted as broken.

keyTerms.meaning: Vows that could not be kept because of circumstances beyond one's control
He bound him with a vow

phrases.english: MISHNAH: Vows blocked by circumstances beyond one's control:
if his friend bound him with a vow that he would eat at his house,
and he got sick, or his son got sick,
or a river held him back,
these are vows blocked by circumstances beyond his control.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה after the earlier discussion of vows with exceptions.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A vow that could not be kept because of sickness or a blocking river counts as נדר אונס.

steps.title: The man who left his documents in court
steps.stepSummary: A man deposited his documents in בית דין and said they should become void if he did not return within thirty days. He was held back by אונס and did not return. רב הונא rules the documents are void.
steps.simpleTranslation: There was a man who left his supporting documents in court and said: If I do not come back within thirty days, let these documents of mine become void. He was held back by circumstances and did not come. רב הונא said: His documents are void.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a real case about a condition a man placed on himself. רב הונא rules that the condition takes effect even though the man was stopped by forces outside his control.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The man set his own deadline, and the deadline passed. רב הונא looks only at the result: the man did not come, so the documents are void, and the reason he did not come does not matter.

keyTerms.meaning: Documents that support one's claim in court
He was held back by circumstances beyond his control

phrases.english: GEMARA: There was a certain man
who deposited his supporting documents in court,
and said: If I do not come
within thirty days,
let these documents of mine be void.
He was held back by circumstances and did not come.
רב הונא said: His documents are void.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָהוּא גַּבְרָא דְּאַתְפֵּיס זָכְווֹתָא בְּבֵי דִינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a real-life case about אונס that will be tested against the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רב הונא, a self-imposed condition takes effect even when it was missed because of אונס.

steps.title: רבא: the תורה exempts someone who was forced
steps.stepSummary: רבא challenges רב הונא: the man is an אנוס, and the תורה exempts an אנוס, as shown by the פסוק about the נערה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to him: He was held back by circumstances, and the Merciful One exempts someone held back by circumstances, as it is written: 'And to the girl you shall do nothing.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבא argues against רב הונא's ruling. He uses a פסוק to show that the תורה does not hold a person responsible for what was forced on him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק is about a נערה who was attacked against her will, and the תורה says she is not punished. רבא learns from this a general rule: אונס רחמנא פטריה. So the man's missed deadline should not count against him.

keyTerms.meaning: Someone forced or held back by circumstances beyond his control
The Merciful One, meaning the תורה or ה׳

phrases.english: רבא said to him:
He was held back by circumstances,
and the Merciful One exempts someone held back by circumstances,
as it is written:
'And to the girl you shall do nothing.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly attacks רב הונא's ruling in step 8.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא's ruling that the documents are void.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The תורה exempts an אנוס, so a condition missed because of אונס should not take effect.

steps.title: Proof from the משנה that the rule is not only for death
steps.stepSummary: רבא heads off an objection that the death penalty might be a special case. He proves from our משנה that אונס exempts a person even in ordinary vows.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say a death penalty is different, didn't we learn in the משנה: What are vows blocked by circumstances? If his friend bound him with a vow to eat at his house, and he got sick, or his son got sick, or a river held him back, these are vows blocked by circumstances!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא expects someone to say the פסוק only applies to death-penalty cases. It answers by bringing back our משנה, which uses the same idea of אונס for a simple vow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone could argue: maybe the תורה is lenient only when a life is at stake. But the משנה says a vow missed because of sickness or a river is a נדר אונס, so אונס exempts a person even in everyday matters. That supports רבא against רב הונא.

keyTerms.meaning: But didn't we learn in a משנה?

steps.confusionAlert: The משנה text is repeated here word for word on purpose. It is not a new משנה. The גמרא is quoting it now as proof for רבא.
steps.whatToRemember: רבא's principle is that אונס exempts a person. It applies beyond capital cases, as the משנה about vows blocked by sickness or a river shows.

phrases.english: And if you would say that a death penalty is different,
but didn't we learn:

phrases.aramaic: נִדְרֵי אוֹנָסִין, הִדִּירוֹ חֲבֵירוֹ שֶׁיֹּאכַל אֶצְלוֹ,
phrases.english: Vows blocked by circumstances: if his friend bound him with a vow that he would eat at his house,
and he got sick, or his son got sick,
or a river held him back,
these are vows blocked by circumstances!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Strengthens רבא's challenge in step 9 by blocking a possible way to limit it.
steps.raayaObject: That the exemption for אונס applies even outside capital cases.
steps.raayaSupportSource: Our משנה, which treats a vow missed because of sickness or a river as נדר אונס.

steps.title: A challenge to רבא from a conditional גט where the husband died
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how רבא's rule fits a משנה in גיטין. There, a husband's conditional גט takes effect even though he died, which is the ultimate אונס.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to רבא, how is this different from what we learned in a משנה: a man said, 'This is your גט from now if I do not come back within twelve months,' and he died within the twelve months. The גט is valid. Why? He was held back by אונס!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבא. It brings a משנה where a condition takes effect even though the person failed because of אונס.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא said a person who fails a condition because of אונס is treated as if he never failed. Death is the strongest kind of אונס, yet the משנה says the גט works. That sounds like the משנה ignores the אונס, which goes against רבא.

keyTerms.meaning: According to רבא, what is the difference? This is a way of asking how his view fits a source
That we learned in a משנה
From now. The גט takes effect starting at the moment it is given
He was truly forced and held back by circumstances he could not control

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the husband simply chose not to come back. He failed to return only because he died. That is exactly why it looks like an אונס that, according to רבא, should cancel the condition.

phrases.english: And according to Rava, what is different
from that which we learned in a mishna:
phrases.notes: This is a משנה in גיטין, about a גט with a condition.

phrases.english: "This is your bill of divorce from now
if I do not arrive from now
until twelve months,"
and he died within twelve months
— this is a valid bill of divorce.
Why? But he was held back by circumstances beyond his control!
phrases.notes: Dying is the clearest case of something a person can't control. That's why it counts as אונס here.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the principle רבא just proved, that אונס exempts a person, using a משנה where it seems not to.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's principle that אונס cancels the effect of a failed condition
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In the גט case, death (the ultimate אונס) stopped the husband from returning, yet the condition still takes effect and the גט is valid. This contradicts רבא's rule.

steps.title: The start of an answer: the גט case may be different
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins to defend רבא by suggesting that the גט case is a special situation.
steps.simpleTranslation: They say: perhaps it is different there.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts to answer the challenge. This line only opens the answer, and the reason the גט case is different comes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא does not reject רבא's rule. Instead it plans to show that the גט case has some special feature, so it is not a true counter-example. The explanation of what makes it different continues in the next lines.

keyTerms.meaning: They say. This often introduces an answer

phrases.english: They say: perhaps it is different there,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins answering the challenge from step 11 by setting the גט case apart.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the cases. The גט case is set apart as special (the full reason continues in the following text).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The גט case shows that אונס does not cancel a condition, which goes against רבא.
steps.terutzMaskana: The גט case may have a special reason, so it does not disprove רבא's general rule.
